summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC scoping focused on quality evaluation and load benchmarks. Discussed success criteria (latency SLO, hallucination rate, precision on extraction tasks), workload sizing, golden prompt construction, regression test design, and timeline for pilot. Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: Deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
questions: What are your strict latency SLOs vs. cost targets?
Do you need data residency / KMS / SOC 2 evidence up front?
Which stakeholders will approve acceptance criteria?
transcript: [00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan from Redwood, AE. Well run about 50 minutes, want to map success criteria and sizing for the POC. Priya from infra will cover benchmarks.
transcript_continued:
[00:18] Priya: Hi! Priya Natarajan, SE. Quick note: we'll propose an initial benchmark that tests both steady state and burst traffic, exercise KV cache, batching and quantization modes. Misspelled sometimes as K V cash in auto transcribes, sorry.
[00:34] Evan: Hi all — Evan Ruiz, Head of ML at Mnemosyne. Our main goals are: accuracy on entity extraction, low hallucination for compliance answers, and sub-350ms median latency for 1K qps. Cost target is a secondary filter.
[00:52] Sofia: Sofia Park, PM. Timeline is tight: need evaluation and exec sign-off within 6 weeks. We also need audit logs for any privacy-related tokens.
[01:10] Liam: Liam O'Neill, infra. I will handle networking and security. We'll likely prefer VPC with customer KMS; may consider on-prem for certain regs.
[01:27] Jordan: Great. High level we proposed a 6-week POC: week 1 onboarding + golden set, week 2-3 bench runs, week 4 regression and hallucination checks, week 5-6 integration and signoff. That okay?
[01:45] Evan: Yes but can we tighten to 5? Exec wants faster. Also how do you measure hallucination precisely?
[02:00] Priya: Good question. We typically do a combination: deterministic format checks (schema matching), semantic hallucination heuristics (comparing outputs against knowledge base), and human review sampling. We'll instrument hallucination rate as percent of outputs that fail QA checks over the golden set.
[02:20] Jordan: For success criteria let's be explicit: latency median under 350ms, p95 under 900ms, hallucination under 2% on golden set, extraction F1 > 0.88, and no critical security gaps. Are those realistic?
[02:40] Evan: F1 0.88 seems fine. Hallucination 2% is aggressive but okay as a target.
[02:48] Sofia: Also need format conformance 99% — like the JSON schema our downstream uses.
[03:02] Priya: We'll add automated format checks in the regression suite. If the model returns free text instead of the structured field, it fails the format gate.
[03:18] Jordan: On workload, can you describe expected traffic? steady qps, spike pattern, average prompt length?
[03:28] Liam: Steady 200 qps during business hours, 1k qps burst for 10-minute windows twice a day, and long-tail of async batched batch jobs at night. Average prompt ~ 120 tokens, max 1,024 tokens for some documents.
[03:50] Priya: Good. For benchmarks we'll simulate 200 qps steady and 1k qps spikes, plus long-sequence runs. We'll run both hosted and a Dedicated setup to compare cost/latency tradeoffs. Note: Redwood Dedicated was called Redwood Dedicate in an earlier doc, transcripts sometimes munged that.
[04:12] Evan: For Dedicated, we need an estimate of reserved capacity and burst pricing—can you include that in the pricing doc?
[04:20] Jordan: Yes, we'll send both on-demand hosted pricing and dedicated reserved capacity options with burst allowances.
[04:29] Sofia: For golden prompts: we can provide 5k seed prompts focusing on edge cases and high-regret scenarios. We need guidance on how to craft golden outputs.
[04:40] Priya: We'll share a golden prompt template: each row should include input, expected structured output, tolerance (exact/soft), tags (hallucination-prone, extraction, summarization). Golden outputs should be the canonical expected answer.
[04:58] Evan: How about regression tests? We need nightly runs and pre-rollout checks.
[05:06] Priya: Regression suite will include: full golden set run (5k) weekly, smoke regression on a prioritized 500-case set for nightly, and a canary pass for any model change. We'll surface diffs and a scoring dashboard.
[05:26] Jordan: Scoring approach — we'll combine metrics into a composite score: 50% task accuracy (F1/precision), 20% hallucination penalty, 20% latency penalty, 10% format compliance. You can tune weights. Does that align?
[05:44] Evan: Yes. Could you show an example calculation?
[05:50] Priya: Sure. Example: F1=0.9 -> 45 points, hallucination 1% -> small penalty -> 19.8, latency med 320ms -> near top -> 18, format 99% -> 9.9. Composite 92.7 — above pass threshold of 85.
[06:19] Sofia: Who signs off? Is it product + security?
[06:24] Jordan: Typically product + ML lead + security. We'll document the acceptance sign-off in the POC success criteria doc.
[06:34] Liam: Regarding security: SOC 2 and ISO are must-haves, SSO with SAML, RBAC, and audit logs. For Private we need customer KMS and HSM integration.
[06:48] Priya: We support SAML SSO, RBAC, and can integrate with customer KMS. We'll include audit-log retention details in the security appendix.
[07:02] Evan: Any limits on prompt caching? We use prefix reuse heavily. How does Redwood handle KV cache?
[07:10] Priya: Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching. For POC we'll test cache hit rates. Note: some transcripts show KV "cash" or "K V cash" and that's an auto transcription artifact.
[07:25] Jordan: For hallucination detection, Priya suggested both automated heuristics and human sampling. Can you expand on heuristics?
[07:34] Priya: Heuristics include cross-checks against an internal knowledge base, named-entity validation, and anchor phrase matching. For example, if the model claims a regulation exists, we check for a match in the KB; if not found, flag for human review. We'll also do n-gram overlap checks against golden outputs.
[07:56] Evan: Do you provide tooling to label hallucinations or do we need to instrument our own UI?
[08:03] Priya: We provide a lightweight review UI for annotation during the POC; customers can also push annotations via an API into the regression harness.
[08:15] Sofia: For scoring thresholds, can we set hard gates that block rollout? Like if hallucination > 3% then fail.
[08:24] Jordan: Absolutely — we'll codify gates in the rollout policy. You can have hard gates (fail) or soft gates (alert).
[08:33] Liam: About observability, we need per-route token-level cost, latency breakdown, and error traces. Is that in Redwood Console?
[08:41] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console shows token breakdowns, per-model trace links, and a trace per request. We'll enable extended retention for the POC logs if needed.
[08:54] Evan: Okay, let's talk acceptance data: do you require sample production traffic or can we use synthetic datasets?
[09:01] Jordan: Synthetic is fine for initial eval, but for final acceptance we prefer a slice of production-like traffic to validate tail latencies and real-world prompts.
[09:13] Sofia: We'll provide sanitized production slices. Need guidance on what to sanitize.
[09:18] Priya: Remove PII and any regulated fields; we'll outline the sanitization checklist. Also, if you need air-gapped/on-prem options we can discuss Private deployment which includes customer-managed network.
[09:32] Evan: What about costs of running the benchmark — is Redwood covering that or we need to allocate cloud credits?
[09:38] Jordan: For initial POC runs we often provide some hosted credits; heavy Dedicated benchmarking may require a temporary trial commitment or cost-sharing which we'll specify in the pricing doc.
[09:51] Liam: On-network egress and peering, we need to confirm allowed endpoints. I'll share ours.
[09:58] Jordan: Perfect. Now, about golden prompt construction — can we walk through an example?
[10:05] Priya: Example row: input: "Extract patient-medication pairs from note", expected_output: {"medications": ["aspirin"]}, tolerance: exact, tags: [extraction, high-risk]. We'll attach a CSV template.
[10:25] Evan: For edge cases we have paraphrases and ambiguous references; how do you handle oracle answers when multiple answers could be correct?
[10:33] Priya: In that case, annotate golden outputs with accepted variants and use a soft match scoring. We'll show example matching logic in the rubric.
[10:45] Sofia: How do you handle partial credit in scoring? For example, extracting 2/3 entities correctly.
transcript_continued_2:
[10:52] Priya: We'll score at the field level and compute micro-averaged F1. Partial credit rolls up into the composite accuracy metric.
[11:05] Evan: For hallucination labelling, is it binary or graded?
[11:10] Priya: Usually binary at the sample level for the gate, and graded for root-cause analysis (minor hallucination vs factual error).
[11:20] Jordan: Let's finalize the regression cadence: nightly smoke, weekly full golden run, and ad-hoc before any major model switch.
[11:31] Sofia: Can the POC include model variant comparisons? We want to test a smaller quantized model vs a larger one to see cost tradeoffs.
[11:38] Priya: Yes — we'll include at least three variants: base open model, quantized variant, and a tuned model if you want. We'll run side-by-side A/B with identical prompts.
[11:52] Evan: Good. Any gating on hallucination because smaller models might hallucinate more.
[11:58] Priya: We'll capture hallucination delta and include in the cost-vs-quality sheet.
[12:06] Liam: For Private deployment, what's the onboarding time?
[12:11] Jordan: Private typically takes 4-8 weeks depending on network and KMS approvals; Dedicated trial is faster, about 1-2 weeks to provision trial capacity.
[12:25] Sofia: Given our timeline, we might start with hosted + dedicated trial in parallel.
[12:31] Jordan: Good approach. We'll craft a timeline in the POC doc with parallel tasks.
[12:38] Evan: Regarding eval metrics, can we get raw per-sample logs so we can run our own analysis?
[12:44] Priya: Yes — we'll provide raw output logs, token-level timing, and scoring outputs. We'll redact anything needing sanitization.
[12:54] Sofia: For the dashboard, can you show regression diffs per test case?
[12:59] Priya: Dashboard supports per-case diffs and can link to the review UI showing golden vs candidate.
[13:09] Jordan: We're near the 15 minute marker in our notes; quick check on risks: network approvals, KMS timelines, and golden set completeness. Any other blockers?
[13:22] Liam: Legal wants a data processing addendum for PII handling, will flag that.
[13:29] Evan: Also need clarity on model updates mid-POC — do you allow rolling model upgrades?
[13:35] Priya: We recommend freezing the model for acceptance runs; for other exploratory tests we can run multiple models but acceptance is against the pinned model and config.
[13:48] Sofia: For the scoring approach, can we tweak the composite weights during the POC?
[13:52] Jordan: Yes, weights are configurable; we typically agree baseline weights and then adjust if the product team requests different priorities.
[14:05] Evan: How will you detect regressions in hallucination specifically — is there an automated diff?
[14:11] Priya: We compare hallucination flags per case across model versions and compute delta; cases with new hallucinations are triaged.
[14:21] Jordan: All right let's capture the deliverables: 1) POC success criteria doc, 2) benchmark plan and runbook, 3) golden prompt template and example 100-case set, 4) security appendix, 5) pricing options. We'll send by Friday.
[14:42] Evan: Sounds good. Any other technical deep-dive items we should do now or schedule?
[14:48] Priya: We should schedule a 90-minute deep dive on the benchmark harness and observability with your infra team — recommend next week.
[14:56] Liam: Next week works. I'll invite infra and SRE.
[15:02] Sofia: One more thing: can you include example failure remediation playbooks? e.g., if hallucination spikes in production, what's the fallback?
[15:11] Priya: Yes — we'll include automatic fallback policies: route to smaller model for cost, route to cached responses for known prompts, or fall back to safe-answer templates. Also mention circuit-breaker thresholds.
[15:28] Evan: Good. For acceptance, can we codify the pass/fail criteria in the doc so legal and finance can review?
[15:35] Jordan: We'll include a one-page acceptance table with metrics and thresholds for signoff.
[15:41] Sofia: Okay, done. Any competitors you want to call out? We experimented with Anthropic and saw different hallucination profiles.
[15:50] Jordan: Noted; we'll include a competitor appendix comparing the results we've seen historically.
[15:58] Evan: Last logistical Q: where do we upload artifacts?
[16:02] Jordan: We'll share a Google Drive folder and the benchmark sheet; for sensitive logs we'll use an S3 bucket w/ pre-signed URLs — we'll share access controls.
[16:13] Priya: I'll also create the initial GitHub repo with the harness and example YAML.
transcript_continued_3:
[16:25] Jordan: Let's recap next steps — Jordan to send docs, Priya to set up bench run template, Evan to deliver golden prompts, Liam to confirm network/KMS. Anything else?
[16:36] Evan: We'll try to have golden prompts earlier if possible.
[16:40] Sofia: I'll coordinate signoff parties and calendar.
[16:45] Liam: I'll open a security ticket for the DPA and KMS approvals.
[16:50] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the infra deep-dive and the benchmark run.
[16:57] Evan: Thanks folks.
[16:59] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[17:02] Jordan: Bye.

Notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (Redwood Dedicate/Dedicated, KV cash/KV cache). Some spoken times omitted; timestamps approximate.
